scope: Only the IR global/header load hoisting portion, adapted to Dewy operand views and restricted to release. No descending loops or affine-index decomposition imported.
patch:
--- a/core/compiler/loops.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/loops.jo
@@ -549,6 +549,198 @@
         if ins.op == .loop: has_loop = true
     if floats and has_loop: loop_versioning(true)
 
+# ---------------- hoisting loads of globals ----------------
+# An innermost loop that calls nothing and stores only where no global variable is (the stack,
+# or objects reached through pointers read from globals or the heap) leaves the globals as they
+# are: their values are read once in front of it, and then the headers (lengths) of what they
+# hold, when the loop does not write headers either (guarded: a null array has none, and the
+# loop reads one only past its own null test). Top-level code, whose variables are all globals,
+# then gets its checks dropped by versioning as a function's locals do.
+lh_ndef: int[]
+lh_defpos: int[]
+lh_raw = false                 # (the function reads or writes through raw pointers: only stores through
+                               # an array or string global count as the heap's)
+
+# is v defined once, by an instruction (a parameter or a vreg defined several times: no)
+lh_def = (code: Ins[], v: int) -> int:
+    if v < 0 or v >= lh_ndef.len() or is_kv(v) or lh_ndef[v] != 1: return -1
+    lh_defpos[v]
+
+# the address v is that of a global variable (its own storage, plus a constant)
+lh_global_addr = (code: Ins[], v0: int) -> bool:
+    v = v0
+    loop k in [0..8):
+        p = lh_def(code, v)
+        if p < 0: return false
+        ins = code[p]
+        if ins.op == .gaddr: return true
+        if ins.op == .mov: v = int(ins.a)
+        else if ins.op == .add and is_kv(int(ins.b)): v = int(ins.a)
+        else: return false
+    false
+
+# a pointer read from a global or from the heap (not from the stack, which may hold a pointer to a
+# global, as a `mut` parameter's): an object's, never a global variable's own storage
+lh_heap_ptr = (code: Ins[], v: int, depth: int) -> bool:
+    p = lh_def(code, v)
+    if p < 0 or depth > 8: return false
+    ins = code[p]
+    if ins.op == .mov: return lh_heap_ptr(code, int(ins.a), depth + 1)
+    if ins.op != .load or int(ins.c) & M_HDR != 0: return false
+    a = int(ins.a)
+    if lh_raw:
+        q = lh_def(code, a)
+        return q >= 0 and code[q].op == .gaddr and obj_global_offs.contains(code[q].imm)
+    lh_global_addr(code, a) or lh_heap_addr(code, a, depth + 1)
+
+# an address in an object reached through such a pointer
+lh_heap_addr = (code: Ins[], v: int, depth: int) -> bool:
+    p = lh_def(code, v)
+    if p < 0 or depth > 8: return false
+    ins = code[p]
+    if ins.op == .add and is_kv(int(ins.b)): return lh_heap_addr(code, int(ins.a), depth + 1)
+    if ins.op == .mov: return lh_heap_addr(code, int(ins.a), depth + 1)
+    lh_heap_ptr(code, v, depth)
+
+# may a store to address v write a global variable?
+lh_safe_store = (code: Ins[], v: int) -> bool:
+    p = lh_def(code, v)
+    if p < 0: return false
+    op = code[p].op
+    if op == .slot: return true
+    if (op == .add and is_kv(int(code[p].b))) or op == .mov:
+        q = lh_def(code, int(code[p].a))
+        if q >= 0 and code[q].op == .slot: return true
+    lh_heap_addr(code, v, 0)
+
+lh_mark: int[]             # per vreg: what the loop being looked at does with it (lx_hoist)
+const LH_BIG = 1000000000
+
+lh_prepare = (code: Ins[]):
+    nv = ir.vtypes.len()
+    lh_ndef = fill(0, nv)
+    lh_defpos = fill(-1, nv)
+    loop q in 0.. and qi in code:
+        d = int(qi.dst)
+        if d >= 0 and o_defines(qi.op):
+            lh_ndef[d] += 1
+            lh_defpos[d] = q
+        if qi.op == .zeroslots:
+            loop k in [0..int(qi.b)):
+                item = int(ir.args[int(qi.a) + k])
+                if item & 1 == 1: lh_ndef[item >> 1] += 2
+    lh_mark = fill(0, nv)
+
+# the loops of cl that have checks (and nothing that may write a global) get the loads moved
+# in front of them; true if any did
+lx_hoist = (cl: CLoop[]) -> bool:
+    lh_raw = ir.raw_mem
+    code = ir.code
+    hoists: (int, int[])[]          # (loop position, what moves in front of it: positions, a
+                                    # negative one a header load, guarded)
+    moved: bool[]
+    ready = false
+    loop L in cl:
+        pl = L.pl
+        pe = L.pe
+        # (first what is quick to see: calls, checks, and something to move)
+        ok = true
+        checks = 0
+        loads = false
+        stores = false
+        loop p in [pl + 1..pe):
+            op = code[p].op
+            if op == .calli or op == .callc or op == .syscall or op == .intr or op == .vop or op == .vst:
+                ok = false
+                break
+            if op == .call:
+                if code[p].c != 1:
+                    ok = false
+                    break
+                checks += 1
+            else if op == .gaddr or (op == .load and int(code[p].c) & M_INDEX == 0): loads = true
+            else if op == .store or op == .copy or op == .zero or op == .memcpy or op == .memset: stores = true
+        if not ok or checks == 0 or not loads: continue
+        if not ready:
+            # (definitions: counted once, for the first loop that needs them)
+            ready = true
+            lh_prepare(code)
+            moved = fill(false, code.len())
+        hdr_ok = true
+        if stores:
+            loop p in [pl + 1..pe):
+                op = code[p].op
+                if op == .store or op == .copy or op == .zero or op == .memcpy or op == .memset:
+                    ins = code[p]
+                    if not lh_safe_store(code, int(ins.a)):
+                        ok = false
+                        break
+                    if op == .store and int(ins.c) & M_HDR != 0: hdr_ok = false
+                    if op != .store:
+                        q = lh_def(code, int(ins.a))
+                        if q < 0 or code[q].op != .slot: hdr_ok = false
+        if not ok: continue
+        # (marks for this loop: lm defined in it, lm + BIG also read before that (or cleared by
+        # zeroslots), -lm only read in it)
+        lm = pl + 1
+        loop p in [pl + 1..pe):
+            ins = code[p]
+            d = ir_operands(ins)
+            loop operand_index in [0..ir_use_count):
+                u = ir_use(operand_index)
+                m = lh_mark[u]
+                if m != lm and m != -lm and m != lm + LH_BIG: lh_mark[u] = -lm
+            if d >= 0:
+                if lh_mark[d] == -lm: lh_mark[d] = lm + LH_BIG
+                else if lh_mark[d] != lm + LH_BIG: lh_mark[d] = lm
+            if ins.op == .zeroslots:
+                loop k in [0..int(ins.b)):
+                    item = int(ir.args[int(ins.a) + k])
+                    if item & 1 == 1: lh_mark[item >> 1] = lm + LH_BIG
+        hs: int[]
+        loop p in [pl + 1..pe):
+            ins = code[p]
+            d = int(ins.dst)
+            if d < 0 or not o_defines(ins.op) or lh_ndef[d] != 1 or lh_mark[d] != lm: continue
+            a = int(ins.a)
+            inl = a >= 0 and (lh_mark[a] == lm or lh_mark[a] == lm + LH_BIG)
+            if ins.op == .gaddr:
+                hs.push(p)
+                lh_mark[d] = 0
+            else if ins.op == .load and int(ins.c) & (M_INDEX | M_HDR) == 0 and not inl and lh_global_addr(code, a):
+                hs.push(p)
+                lh_mark[d] = 0
+            else if ins.op == .load and hdr_ok and int(ins.c) & M_INDEX == 0 and int(ins.c) & M_HDR != 0 and not inl:
+                hs.push(-p - 1)
+                lh_mark[d] = 0
+        if hs.len() == 0: continue
+        hoists.push((pl, hs))
+        loop h in hs:
+            if h >= 0: moved[h] = true
+            else: moved[-h - 1] = true
+    if hoists.len() == 0: return false
+    out: Ins[]
+    out.reserve(code.len() + 16)
+    hk = 0
+    loop p in 0.. and ins in code:
+        if moved[p]: continue
+        if hk < hoists.len() and hoists[hk].0 == p:
+            loop h in hoists[hk].1:
+                if h >= 0: out.push(code[h])
+                else:
+                    hi = code[-h - 1]
+                    # d = 0; if a != 0: d = load a
+                    out.push(Ins(.mov, VI, hi.dst, i32(k_vreg(0)), 0, 0, 0))
+                    t = vreg(VI)
+                    out.push(Ins(.ne, VI, i32(t), hi.a, i32(k_vreg(0)), 0, 0))
+                    out.push(Ins(.if_, 0, 0, i32(t), 0, 0, 0))
+                    out.push(hi)
+                    out.push(Ins(.end, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0))
+            hk += 1
+        out.push(ins)
+    ir.code = out
+    true
+
 # version the counting loops of the current function that have checks to drop
 lx_dbg_read = false
 lx_dbg = ""
@@ -561,6 +753,10 @@
     ends = lx_ends(code)
     cl = lx_counting(code, ends)
     if cl.len() == 0: return
+    if not vector_only and lx_hoist(cl):
+        code = ir.code
+        ends = lx_ends(code)
+        cl = lx_counting(code, ends)
     nv = ir.vtypes.len()
     lx_known = 0
     lx_sync()
--- a/core/compiler/lower.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/lower.jo
@@ -47,6 +47,7 @@
 ffi_slot: {int: int} = {}       # offset -> index
 glsl_of: {int: str} = {}        # (sloppy watch) shader() node -> the GLSL made for it
 global_off: {int: int} = {}
+obj_global_offs: {int: bool} = {} # array/string globals hold objects, never global storage addresses
 entry_points: int[]
 
 # relocations inside rodata/data that hold function addresses or data addresses are not needed:
@@ -116,6 +117,8 @@
     if sz < 8: sz = 8
     data_size += sz
     global_off[g] = o
+    tk = types[prune(t)].kind
+    if tk == .array or tk == .str_: obj_global_offs[o] = true
     o
 
 # ---------------- type helpers ----------------
decision: No useful change on three Dewy pilots: read-only global arrays, array updates, and raw-buffer updates. Each produces identical previous/candidate IR in both modes; small timing differences are not an optimization win. Do not add another analysis pass without a demonstrated customer. Independent C bootstrap, full suite, compiler-speed comparison, and full stage gate were not run for this prototype.
